description: Armor that grew instead of being forged. Spears skate off its plates; its tusks do not return the favor.
lore: [[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] calls it a cheat. Everyone laughs, and she is not joking. She has given a working life to the shoulder — the gap a plate harness has to leave so the arm can go up, and therefore the gap everything gets in through. Every smith who ever lived has failed at the shoulder. This animal wears bands that slide across one another when it breathes and shut when it turns, and it earned none of them, and does not know it has them.

She has been out to look at one four times now, taking no tools, getting no nearer than she has to, standing there watching a beast breathe — the least Sigrun-like thing she does all year. The tusks curve out low and forward and they are built for lifting; what they lift is whatever was standing in front of it. She has not made a shoulder yet.

Understand what she is actually trying to build. Nothing out here can be ended with a spear, so people take plate for vanity. Sigrun has watched what a bad shoulder really costs: a person goes down, re-forms by the nearest fire some hours later, and comes back short a little of what they were thinking — a face, a stretch of road, a name that gave them no trouble last year. It is not a wound. It is a subtraction, it does not come back, and they turn up at her door afterwards unable to say quite why they came. That thing out on the plain has never lost one thought to a spear in its life. She goes back next week.
gm_notes: The funny one that turns: a smith's professional grudge against an animal, played for the joke and then cashed in. Establishes what armour is FOR in a world where nothing dies — it protects memory, not life — which is Law III demonstrated rather than stated, and gives the smithing trade a reason to exist. Sigrun without a refusal scene this time (tree_stump has that); here she is beaten by the problem and returning to it.
